Organic aciduria; developmental impairment, seizures and spasticity occur in 80–99%. Cardiac, hepatic, ocular and hearing abnormalities are each <30%.
Proteus bacterial infection; urinary infections predominate clinically, but this unrestricted concept does not establish common direct urinary organ damage.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the stomach; no additional organ involvement established.
Bile duct inflammation, usually infectious or immune-mediated; biliary structures belong to the hepatic axis.
Lymphoid hematologic proliferations, predominantly lymphomas and immune-associated lymphoproliferative disorders; no common extranodal organ established.
UV-induced skin injury and chronic pigmentary changes define this photodermatosis; DNA repair deficiency alone does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Respiratory-chain metabolic deficiency; muscle dysfunction in 3/3 and proximal weakness in 2/3 support myopathy. Cardiac and renal damage frequencies are unspecified.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma directly infiltrating skin and hair follicles; lymphoma supplies the hematologic and immune mechanism axes.
Inherited actinic porokeratosis is a disorder of cutaneous keratinization.
Acromesomelic osteochondrodysplasia affects limb bone growth and structure; no additional organ involvement established.
Microcephaly and developmental/intellectual impairment define the syndrome. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage; ocular/endocrine frequencies unspecified.
Inherited sideroblastic anemia affects erythropoiesis; elevated ferritin and transferrin saturation do not alone demonstrate hepatic or cardiac injury.
Interferon-mediated immune disease; chronic chilblain skin lesions are common (≥30%). Neurologic injury varies substantially between AGS5 and chilblain-lupus presentations.
Idiopathic anterior uveitis is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the anterior uvea; no systemic organ disease is specified.
Rare craniofacial malformation involving skull and facial skeletal structure; insufficient evidence for common functional damage to other axes.
Craniosynostosis, radioulnar synostosis and congenital aortic valve disease are the explicitly defining structural phenotypes.
Defining neural tube defects, oral clefts/omphalocele and diaphragmatic muscle defects; diaphragmatic hernia occurs in 30–79%. Renal/cardiac anomalies are <30%.
Joubert cerebellar malformation defines disease; rod-cone dystrophy occurs in 4/4. Individual renal lesions occur in 1/4; recurrent UTIs are separate infections.
Developmental and intellectual impairment predominate across 3q deletion syndromes; ocular, skeletal and cardiac abnormalities depend on the deleted interval.
Congenital cardiac laterality abnormality: dextrocardia in 5/7. Situs reversal alone does not imply visceral damage; asplenia and otitis are <30%; infertility has no axis.
Congenital non-neoplastic skin or adjacent mucosal lesion; no common additional organ involvement.
Malignant B-lymphoblast proliferation defines leukemia/lymphoma; no additional organ has established common direct injury.
Hereditary demyelinating peripheral motor and sensory neuropathy; weakness reflects nerve dysfunction rather than primary muscle damage.
